{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''William Frederick Eberlein''' (June 25, 1917, [[Shawano, Wisconsin]] – 1986, [[Rochester, New York]]) was an American mathematician, specializing in mathematical analysis and mathematical physics.

==Life==
Eberlein studied from 1936 to 1942 at the [[University of Wisconsin]] and at [[Harvard University]], where he received in 1942 a PhD for the thesis ''Closure, Convexity, and Linearity in Banach Spaces'' under the direction of [[Marshall Harvey Stone|Marshall Stone]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=7641}}</ref>

He was married twice—to Mary Bernarda Barry and Patricia Ramsay James. He had four children with Mary Barry, including Patrick Barry Eberlein, another renowned mathematician. Patricia Ramsay James was a mathematician who moved into computer science as the field opened up; their one child is Kristen James Eberlein, the chair of the OASIS [[Darwin Information Typing Architecture]] Technical Committee.

==Work==
Eberlein had academic positions at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] (1947–1948), at the University of Wisconsin (1948–1955), at [[Wayne State University]] (1955–1956), and from 1957 at the [[University of Rochester]], where he remained for the rest of his career.<ref name="briscoe">[https://txarchives.org/utcah/finding_aids/00191.xml W. F. Eberlein Papers, 1936–1986], Briscoe Center for American History, University of Texas at Austin, retrieved 2023-11-04.</ref> His doctoral students include [[William F. Donoghue, Jr.]]<ref>{{cite web|author=Gelbaum, Bernard Russell|author-link=Bernard Russell Gelbaum|title=In Memoriam: William F. Donoghue, Jr.|website=University of California|url=https://senate.universityofcalifornia.edu/_files/inmemoriam/html/WilliamF.Donoghue.htm}}</ref> and [[A. Wayne Wymore]].

==Contributions==
He worked on [[functional analysis]], [[harmonic analysis]], [[ergodic theory]], mean value theorems, and [[numerical integration]]. Eberlein also worked on spacetime models, internal symmetries in [[gauge theory]], and [[spinor]]s.<ref name="briscoe"/> His name is attached to the [[Eberlein–Šmulian theorem]] in functional analysis<ref>{{citation|title=A Course in Functional Analysis|volume=96|series=Graduate Texts in Mathematics|first=John B.|last=Conway|author-link=John B. Conway|publisher=Springer|year=1990|isbn=9780387972459|page=163|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ix4P1e6AkeIC&pg=PA163}}.</ref>, the [[Eberlein compacta]] in [[topology]]<ref>{{citation|contribution=Eberlein compacta|title=Encyclopedia of General Topology|editor1-first=K. P.|editor1-last=Hart|editor2-first=Jun-iti|editor2-last=Nagata|editor3-first=J. E.|editor3-last=Vaughan|publisher=Elsevier|year=2003|isbn=9780080530864|pages=145–146|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JWyoCRkLFAkC&pg=PA145|first=A. V.|last=Arhangel'skii|author-link=Alexander Arhangelskii}}.</ref>, and the Eberlein mean ergodic theorem<ref>{{cite book |last1=Krengel |first1=Ulrich |title=Ergodic Theorems |date=1985 |publisher=Walter de Gruyter & Co. |location=Berlin |page=76}}</ref>.
